title: Fonctions L / Équation fonctionnelle des fonctions L (cas géométrique) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not Grothendieck's own mathematics. It is a typed sheet from a Bourbaki draft (header '6 - 33 -', 'n° 392', '§ 4.'), reused as scrap paper inside folder 60, whose surrounding handwritten pages compute functional equations of L-functions (products of factors L_i(p^k t), signs δ, exponents χ). The content is a block of exercises for the Bourbaki Commutative Algebra chapter on divisors (AC VII §4: reflexive lattices, pseudo-null modules, structure of modules over Krull/noetherian normal domains). A is a noetherian integrally closed domain throughout, and a lattice (réseau) is a finitely generated submodule of V spanning V.

(1) Any intersection of reflexive lattices M_λ in V that all contain a fixed lattice N is again a reflexive lattice. M is a lattice because N ⊂ M ⊂ M_λ. Each M_λ equals ∩_{ht p=1} (M_λ)_p, so M = ∩_p M_p is reflexive. The hint is to use the dual lattices M_λ^*: M is the dual of the lattice generated by the M_λ^*, which is contained in N^*.

(2) Let E be torsion-free and F finitely generated, with Hom(E,F) reflexive and Ext^1(E,F)=0. Then F is reflexive. First one shows F is torsion-free. Then set T = F^{**}/c_F(F). The sequence 0 → Hom(E,F) → Hom(E,F^{**}) → Hom(E,T) → 0 is exact because Ext^1 vanishes. Compute Ass(Hom(E,T)) in two ways. On one side it is Supp(E) ∩ Ass(T), which consists of primes of height ≥ 2. On the other side, Hom(E,T) embeds in Ext^1-type data of reflexive modules, so its associated primes have height ≤ 1. Hence T = 0.

(3) If M is a reflexive lattice contained in a free lattice L, then M = L ∩ L_1 for some free lattice L_1. Let I be the finite set of height-one primes p with M_p ≠ L_p. The semilocal Dedekind ring S^{-1}A is principal. So there is a free L_0 with (L_0)_p = M_p for all p in I. Then take L_1 = s^{-1}L_0 with s ∈ S.

(4a) Over k[X,Y], let E be generated by (X−Y)e_1, e_1+Xe_2, e_1+Ye_2 and F by (X−Y)^2 e_1. Then E/F does not split as torsion ⊕ torsion-free.

(4b) A/(XY) is not a direct sum of modules A/P^n with P prime of height 1. It is indecomposable, being cyclic over a local-at-the-origin situation, yet it has two distinct associated primes.

(5) (aM ∩ bM)/(a∩b)M is pseudo-null. Localize at height ≤ 1 primes: the ring becomes a field or a DVR, the ideals are powers of the uniformizer, and the quotient vanishes. An example where it is nonzero is required.
errors: Ex. 3: 'pour tout p ⊂ I' should read 'p ∈ I' (typo in the typescript).
Ex. 2: the cross-reference 'chap. IV, § 1, n° , prop. ' is left blank in the draft.
